findings.title: MQTT Broker Anonymous Authentication Bypass
findings.evidence: CONNACK return code 0x00 (Connection Accepted) — anonymous access granted.
findings.owasp_category: I1 – Weak, Guessable, or Hardcoded Passwords
findings.remediation:
In mosquitto.conf:
  allow_anonymous false
  password_file /etc/mosquitto/passwd
Then run: mosquitto_passwd -c /etc/mosquitto/passwd <username>

findings.title: MQTT Wildcard Topic Namespace Exposure
findings.evidence: Wildcard '#' subscription succeeded. Topics exposed: telemetry/temp, sensors/node1/accel, status/health
findings.remediation:
Implement MQTT ACLs in mosquitto.conf:
  acl_file /etc/mosquitto/acl
ACL file example:
  user sensor_node
  topic readwrite sensors/#
  topic deny #

findings.title: Unencrypted Cleartext HTTP Admin Interface
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 — web interface accessible over plaintext HTTP (no TLS redirect).
findings.owasp_category: I7 – Insecure Data Transfer and Storage
findings.remediation:
1. Enable HTTPS on the device web server.
2. Add HTTP -> HTTPS redirect (301) for all admin paths.
3. Enforce Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) headers.

findings.title: Exposed Diagnostic / Telemetry Endpoints Without Authentication
findings.remediation:
1. Require Bearer token / Basic Auth over HTTPS on all API paths.
2. Disable diagnostic endpoints in production firmware.

findings.title: Default or Hardcoded Web Interface Credentials
findings.owasp_category: I1 – Weak, Guessable, or Hardcoded Passwords
findings.remediation:
1. Force administrator password rotation on initial boot.
2. Enforce minimum complexity requirements and rate limit login endpoints.

findings.title: Unauthenticated CoAP Resource Discovery (.well-known/core)
findings.evidence: CoAP response code 4.01 — Access denied / authentication enforced.
findings.remediation: Maintain DTLS Pre-Shared Key (PSK) requirement for all CoAP queries.

findings.title: Unauthenticated RTSP Video Stream Access
findings.evidence: RTSP DESCRIBE returned 401/403 on all probed paths — authentication enforced.
findings.owasp_category: I1 – Weak, Guessable, or Hardcoded Passwords
